correctness.rationale: The contextual upper estimate follows from the colliding-pair neighborhood argument in the source. The disjoint subdivided-star bases have precisely one collision (the two centers) and exactly 2d+2 distinct valid singleton repairs; all complement singletons fail domination. The wheel witness has exactly the displayed collision 2,7 and all six omitted vertices repair it. The constructions cover all d>=2 and every m>=10 without extrapolation. Finite brute-force checks support but do not prove the unrestricted statements.

originality.rationale: The motivating manuscript already contains the neighborhood-counting argument implying the contextual 2d+2 apex repair upper bound, and that upper bound is not novel. The new constructive assertions are attainment of 2d+2 in every degree d>=2 together with an LDC partition of 2d+3 classes, and seven-class LDC partitions on every sufficiently long wheel. The full source gives neither construction; literature and mathematical-record searches found no dominating theorem or exact wheel table. Priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: The upper bound alone is an existing method, but universal attainability in every degree d>=2 is a natural exact extremal problem not implied by that bound. A constructive cone family realizes all 2d+2 possible repairs as singleton coalition partners and yields unbounded coalition partition sizes. The seven-class wheel family creates a uniform strict separation from the known cycle six-class ceiling and is not a routine numerical table. These structurally motivated infinite constructions have value independently of the known upper estimate.
